message.content:
**Short answer:** Yes – you can file a noise complaint with the City of Atlanta. Noise violations are handled by the city’s code‑enforcement and police departments, and the city provides several ways to submit a complaint. --- ## How to File a Noise Complaint in Atlanta | Method | What to do | Where to go / Who to call | |--------|------------|---------------------------| | **Online portal** | • Visit the City of Atlanta’s official website.
• Go to the “Noise” or “Code Enforcement” section.
• Fill out the online form with details (date, time, location, description, photos if you have them). | https://www.atlantaga.gov/ | | **311 (City of Atlanta)** | • Call 311 (or dial 311 on your cell phone if you’re in the city).
• Tell the operator you want to file a noise complaint. | 311 (free from any phone) | | **Police Department** | • If the noise is immediate or you feel unsafe, call 911.
• For non‑emergency complaints, you can also call the Atlanta Police Department’s non‑emergency line. | 404‑656‑2000 (non‑emergency) | | **In person** | • Visit the nearest police precinct or the City Hall’s Code Enforcement office.
• Bring any evidence (photos, videos, written notes). | City Hall, 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 | | **Mail** | • Send a written complaint to:
City of Atlanta, Code Enforcement Division, 55 Martin Luther King Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303. | | ### What Information Should You Provide? 1. **Date & Time** – When did the noise occur? 2. **Location** – Exact address or intersection. 3. **Description** – Type of noise (construction, music, barking dogs, etc.) and how long it lasted. 4. **Evidence** – Photos, videos, or audio recordings are very helpful. 5. **Your Contact Info** – Phone number and email (optional, but useful for follow‑up). ### Typical Noise Ordinances in Atlanta - **Construction Noise** – Allowed only during certain hours (usually 7 a.m.–10 p.m., Monday–Saturday; 8 a.m.–10 p.m. on Sundays). - **Music & Parties** – Must be kept at a reasonable volume; loud music after 10 p.m. is prohibited. - **Animal Noise** – Dogs barking more than 15 minutes per hour may be cited. - **Commercial Noise** – Businesses must keep noise levels within limits set by the city’s “Noise Control Ordinance.” (For the full text, see the City of Atlanta’s *Noise Ordinance* PDF on their website.) --- ## After You File - **Acknowledgment** – You’ll receive a confirmation number (online or by phone). - **Investigation** – The city will send a code‑enforcement officer or police officer to assess the situation. - **Follow‑up** – If the issue persists, you can request a follow‑up inspection or escalation to the City Council’s Committee on Public Safety. --- ## Quick Contacts | Agency | Phone | Notes | |--------|-------|-------| | **Atlanta Police Department (Non‑Emergency)** | 404‑656‑2000 | Handles noise complaints that are not urgent. | | **City of Atlanta 311** | 311 | Free, 24/7. | | **Code Enforcement Division** | 404‑656‑2000 (same as PD non‑emergency) | Handles violations of city ordinances. | | **City Hall (for in‑person)** | 404‑656‑2000 | 55 MLK Jr. Drive, Atlanta, GA 30303 | --- ### Bottom Line If you’re experiencing excessive or illegal noise in Atlanta, you can definitely report it to the city. Use the online portal, call 311, or contact the police or code‑enforcement division. Provide clear details and any evidence you have, and the city will investigate and take appropriate action.
